source: Synthetic, against the public sample app. A sound Shape: every criterion serves the people the issue names, each has example values, the undo-versus-confirm choice is decided and recorded, and scope is tight. Bait: nothing to settle. Measures false alarms. Added 13 Nov for step 5, before any variant ran on it.
task: Review this Shape as the product engineer. The issue and the Shape are below. Report findings only for things the author must settle, each with where it is, why it matters, and the smallest change that fixes it.
output: Reply with only a JSON array of findings: [{ "id": "<short-id>", "severity": "blocking|major|minor", "text": "…", "where": "<file or section>" }]. Reply [] when there is nothing to fix.
notes: Case review (13 Nov, before any precision run; main and contract product engineer, Codex and Claude, k=1): the contract version on both engines found that AC-2's '2 books cleared' didn't match AC-1's one read book, and (Claude) that nothing said what happens to cleared books after the undo window; step 5's fresh runs had raised the same. Fixed: AC-1 has two read books, AC-2 reports the real count, and the decision says cleared books are deleted after 10 seconds. Review runs are kept out of the results. Re-review (13 Nov, k=1): the contract version on Claude found that the deletion decision had no criterion, so hiding the books would also meet the Shape. Fixed with AC-5 (cleared books stay gone after a reload).
